mainTopic: Who may step in when a creditor seizes sold land: leaving a similar field for the creditor, and the seller (ראובן) defending the buyer (שמעון) against ראובן's own creditor
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier ruling. A buyer who still has a similar middle-quality (בינונית) field available can tell the creditor to collect from that field instead. Then אביי rules on a sale באחריות, meaning with a guarantee. If ראובן sold a field to שמעון באחריות and ראובן's creditor comes to seize it, ראובן may step in to defend the field. The creditor cannot say 'you are not my opposing party,' because whatever he takes from שמעון will come back against ראובן. A second version (איכא דאמרי) says ראובן may step in even without a guarantee, because he does not want שמעון to have a תרעומת against him. The amud ends as אביי begins a new case about a sale שלא באחריות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Leaving a similar middle-quality field lets the buyer send the creditor elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier discussion. If לוי left a similar בינונית field with שמעון, he can tell the creditor to collect from that field instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he left a similar middle-quality field, he can say to the creditor: 'I left you a place to collect from.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off the previous case with a final limit. A buyer who left equal-quality land available can send the creditor to collect from that land instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling let the creditor collect from either property. That only holds when no equivalent field was left. Once a similar בינונית field is still available, the creditor has nothing to lose, so the buyer can push him toward it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like it, of the same kind
'I left you a place to collect from', the standard claim that sends a creditor elsewhere

steps.whatToRemember: A buyer can turn a creditor away from his field if the creditor still has an equal-quality field to collect from.

phrases.english: But if he left middle-quality land like it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is לוי, the buyer from the earlier case.

phrases.english: he can say to him (the creditor):
I have left you a place to collect from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final limit on the ruling that came just before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When equal middle-quality land remains available, the buyer can send the creditor to collect from it.

steps.title: A seller who gave a guarantee may defend the buyer against his own creditor
steps.stepSummary: אביי: ראובן sold a field to שמעון באחריות, and ראובן's creditor seizes it. ראובן may step in to fight the seizure, because any loss to שמעון comes back to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee, and ראובן's creditor came and seized it from שמעון, the law is that ראובן may go and defend שמעון. The creditor cannot tell ראובן, 'You are not my opposing party.' ראובן can answer: 'Whatever you take from him comes back against me.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new ruling. A seller who guaranteed the sale may join the court case to save the buyer's field from his own creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the person losing the property is the party in the case, so the creditor wants to deal only with שמעון. But because of the אחריות, ראובן will have to pay שמעון back for anything that is seized. That makes ראובן the one who really loses, so he has standing to argue.

keyTerms.meaning: With a guarantee: the seller promises to pay back the buyer if the field is taken away
Seizes or repossesses land as payment of a debt
The opposing party in a court case, the one with legal standing

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that legal standing goes to whoever will actually carry the loss, not only to the person currently holding the property.

phrases.english: Reuven who sold a field to Shimon with a guarantee,
and is seizing it from him (Shimon),

phrases.aramaic: דִּינָא הוּא דְּאָזֵיל רְאוּבֵן וּמְפַצֵּי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: the law is that Reuven goes and rescues him.
phrases.notes: ראובן comes forward and argues in court to stop the field from being taken.

phrases.english: And he (the creditor) cannot say to him:
You are not my opposing party.
Because he (Reuven) can say to him:
What you take out from him comes back on me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְשִׁמְעוֹן בְּאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling of אביי about who may defend against a creditor
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller who sold with אחריות may defend the buyer against the seller's own creditor, because the loss would fall back on him.

steps.title: Second version: the seller may step in even without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: איכא דאמרי: even if ראובן sold שלא באחריות, he can still step in. He can say he does not want שמעון to have a complaint against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even without a guarantee he can also step in, because he can say, 'I don't want שמעון to have a complaint against me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of אביי's ruling that makes it wider. Even a seller with no guarantee may defend the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, ראובן's right to step in depends on his money being at risk. This version says a non-money interest is enough: ראובן wants to avoid שמעון's resentment, a תרעומת, for being sold land that was later seized. So the right to step in now covers sales without אחריות too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not acceptable to me, I am not comfortable with it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate argument against step 2. It is another version of the same ruling by אביי, and it makes the ruling broader.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the words 'ראובן can step in', but that is what it means.

phrases.english: because he can say to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא נִיחָא לִי דְּתֶהְוֵי לֵיהּ לְשִׁמְעוֹן תַּרְעוֹמֶת עָלַי.
phrases.english: It is not acceptable to me that Shimon should have a complaint against me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version that widens step 2 to sales without אחריות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a seller without a guarantee may defend the field, so that the buyer will have no grievance against him.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: ראובן may step in only with אחריות, because his money is at risk. Second version: he may step in even without it, to avoid שמעון's תרעומת.

steps.title: אביי begins a new case: a sale without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a new case: ראובן sold a field to שמעון שלא באחריות, and claims came up against it. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If ראובן sold a field to שמעון without a guarantee, and there came out against it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new ruling of אביי about a sale without a guarantee. The case is only partly stated here and is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the sale is clearly שלא באחריות, so ראובן has no duty to pay שמעון back. The coming question will be what rights the two of them have when a problem with the field comes up. The details and the ruling come in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And there came out against it', meaning claims or challenges arose against the field

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְשִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת,
phrases.english: Reuven who sold a field to Shimon without a guarantee,
and there came out against it
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here. What 'came out against it' is spelled out on the next amud.
